urn:eigenius:core:description: Mathematical-programming institution backed by JuMP.jl with HiGHS as the solver back end. Scope: linear programs and convex quadratic programs (LP / QP). v1 validates `OptimisesTo` claims by rebuilding the JuMP model from the chain-typed `OptimisationProblem` (walking each FormulaTerm under a JuMP-expression interpreter), calling `optimize!`, and comparing the re-solved objective + termination status against the claim within tolerance. Sibling institutions targeting nonlinear programming (Ipopt) and integer programming (HiGHS-MIP, GLPK) ship as separate `Institution` resources reusing the same `OptimisationProblem` shape — only the dispatch package, JuliaEnvironment image, and accepted constraint/objective complexity vary. The smart-pow walker rule (integer-valued `LitFloat` exponent on `pow` unrolls to repeated multiplication) is on by default for this institution because HiGHS does not accept `MOI.ScalarNonlinearFunction` even when the underlying math is quadratic.

Julia entry point that takes an `OptimisesTo` mirror struct and returns a `Verdict`. The handler rebuilds the JuMP model from `claim.problem` (parses variables + bounds, walks objective + each constraint LHS to a JuMP expression with smart-pow on, dispatches `@objective` / `@constraint`), calls `optimize!`, checks `termination_status` against the claim, and tolerance-checks `objective_value`. Variable-value comparison is omitted by design (LP degeneracy). Holds on a successful re-solve that matches; Fails on a status mismatch or objective-value mismatch beyond tolerance; Undecidable on indeterminate solver states (`ITERATION_LIMIT`, `TIME_LIMIT`, `NUMERICAL_ERROR`, `SLOW_PROGRESS`).

AutoOnLoad gate fired against every newly committed `OptimisesTo` resource. Re-solves the referenced problem and produces the canonical D14 Verdict tri-state. A `Fails` verdict rejects the gated commit per D31 §6.3 — the chain only persists OptimisesTo claims whose objective value the institution can independently reproduce.

Julia entry point for the `qc_jump_solve` OnDemand QueryClass. Takes an `OptimisationProblem` and returns an `OptimisesTo` whose `objective_value` / `variable_values` / `termination_status` come from a fresh `optimize!` call. The returned claim's `abstol` / `reltol` are stamped at sensible defaults (1e-6 each) so a downstream AutoOnLoad re-validation gate can run cleanly without the caller having to specify tolerances explicitly. Internally: walks each FormulaTerm under the JuMP-expression interpreter (smart-pow on), constructs a fresh `Model(HiGHS.Optimizer)`, attaches variables + bounds + objective + constraints, optimises, reads back the solution.

OnDemand QueryClass: given an `OptimisationProblem`, solve it via JuMP/HiGHS and return an `OptimisesTo` carrying the optimum. Dispatched explicitly via EigenQL FIBER (D2 v2 §3.5). Useful for parameter-fitting and design-optimisation flows where the chain has the typed problem but doesn't already carry a claimed optimum — the OnDemand call materialises one, which a follow-on commit can record as the chain's recorded optimum (and trigger the AutoOnLoad gate as a re-check).

Julia entry point for the target-side reify of the `Symbolics → JuMP` Comorphism (D14 §9.3 step 4). The comorphism's typed middle is the identity Lambda on `OptimisationProblem` (D32 §6.2 generalised) — both ends speak the same chain shape, so the reify is identity at the boundary. The Julia handler returns its `OptimisationProblem` argument unchanged; the function exists so the kernel's `Exp::InstitutionInvoke` dispatch can route comorphism reify calls through the substrate uniformly with `query` and `extract_typed`, rather than special-casing `no-op` procedures kernel-side.

Typed inbound constructor for `OptimisationProblem`: reifies a FormulaTerm-typed OptimisationProblem payload as itself (identity reify — both source and target speak the same shape). Target side of the `Symbolics → JuMP` comorphism: any institution producing a chain-typed OptimisationProblem (via the FormulaTerm-everywhere story) imports through this format. Anchored on the `reify_problem` Julia handler — the kernel's `ExternalInstitution::reify` dispatches through the substrate the same way `query` does (D14 §9.3 step 4).
